_comment: The scout's long list (scout.md §2.1): LEADS, never a ranking and never facts. Each `edge` is the claim a scout must establish from fetched sources and a re-checker then tries to refute; `start` names where to look first (ids from sources.json, and works to find there). The tier, mode and point of view come only from richness.py over what was fetched. `scout: true` marks the first scout's candidates; the rest wait.

candidates.subject: The Siege of Alesia
candidates.edge: Roman siege engineering: lines of works facing the town and facing outward let a smaller army hold a besieged town and a relief army at once
candidates.pivotal: Ended the Gallic revolt led by Vercingetorix
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, book 7 (an old translation)
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio book 40; Plutarch, Life of Caesar
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar (1865–66 English edition), on the excavations
wikipedia: Battle of Alesia (leads and references only)

candidates.subject: The Siege of Syracuse
candidates.edge: Archimedes' engines held off the Roman assault by land and sea, so Marcellus turned to blockade; the city fell later by an escalade on a festival night
candidates.pivotal: Rome took the greatest Greek city of Sicily; Archimedes was killed
start: gutenberg / internet-archive: Polybius, Histories book 8 (Shuckburgh, 1889)
lacus-curtius: Plutarch, Life of Marcellus
gutenberg: Livy, books 24–25 (an old translation)
wikipedia: Siege of Syracuse (213–212 BC)

candidates.subject: The Battle of the Kalka River
candidates.edge: A Mongol feigned retreat drew the Rus' princes and the Cumans after them for days, into a battle the allies fought piecemeal
candidates.pivotal: The first Mongol defeat of the Rus' princes, fourteen years before the invasion
start: internet-archive: The Chronicle of Novgorod 1016–1471 (Michell and Forbes, 1914)
gutenberg / wikisource: William of Rubruck and John of Plano Carpini (Rockhill, 1900; Beazley, 1903) on Mongol warfare
wikipedia: Battle of the Kalka River

candidates.subject: The Siege of Xiangyang
candidates.edge: Counterweight trebuchets built for the Mongols by engineers from the west broke a five-year siege; the sources disagree about who built them
candidates.pivotal: Opened the Yangtze to the Mongol conquest of the Song
start: gutenberg / internet-archive: The Book of Ser Marco Polo (Yule; Yule–Cordier 1903), with Yule's notes
wikipedia: Battle of Xiangyang

candidates.subject: The Battle of Midway
candidates.edge: Codebreakers at Pearl Harbor read enough of the Japanese naval code to tell Nimitz where and roughly when the attack would come
candidates.pivotal: Four Japanese fleet carriers sunk; the Pacific war's balance at sea shifted
start: hyperwar / navy-nhhc: Office of Naval Intelligence, Combat Narrative: The Battle of Midway (1943)
navy-nhhc: Nimitz's report of the battle
nsa-cch: Frederick D. Parker, A Priceless Advantage (1993)
wikipedia: Battle of Midway

candidates.subject: The Battle of Hampton Roads
candidates.edge: Two ironclads: the Virginia's armour made the wooden blockade fleet helpless, and the Monitor's revolving turret stopped her the next day
candidates.pivotal: The first fight between ironclads; navies began to give up wooden warships
start: internet-archive: Battles and Leaders of the Civil War, vol. 1 (1887): participants' accounts
official-records: Official Records of the Union and Confederate Navies, series 1 vol. 7
navy-nhhc: ship histories
wikipedia: Battle of Hampton Roads

candidates.subject: The Spanish Armada
candidates.edge: English ships built to sail and fire at range, fireships at Calais, then weather and supply, against a fleet built to grapple and board
candidates.pivotal: The invasion of England did not happen
start: internet-archive: Laughton, State Papers Relating to the Defeat of the Spanish Armada (Navy Records Society, 1894): the commanders' letters
gutenberg: Hakluyt's Principal Navigations (the 1588 account)
wikipedia: Spanish Armada

candidates.subject: The Battle of Agincourt
candidates.edge: Longbowmen behind stakes on a narrow, ploughed and rain-soaked field
candidates.pivotal: Henry V's victory led to the Treaty of Troyes
start: internet-archive: Nicolas, History of the Battle of Agincourt (1827), with the chronicles
internet-archive: Gesta Henrici Quinti (Williams, 1850)
wikipedia: Battle of Agincourt

candidates.subject: The Siege of Tyre
candidates.edge: Alexander built a causeway out to an island city and brought rams to its walls on ships
candidates.pivotal: Alexander took the last Persian naval base on the Levant coast
start: gutenberg: Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander (Chinnock)
lacus-curtius: Diodorus book 17; Plutarch, Life of Alexander
wikipedia: Siege of Tyre (332 BC)

candidates.subject: The Battle of Cannae
candidates.edge: Hannibal's double envelopment of a much larger Roman army
candidates.pivotal: Rome's worst defeat; several Italian allies went over to Carthage
start: gutenberg / internet-archive: Polybius book 3 (Shuckburgh, 1889); Livy book 22
wikipedia: Battle of Cannae

candidates.subject: The Berlin Airlift
candidates.edge: A supply system run like a conveyor (fixed altitudes, three-minute spacing, one approach) fed a blockaded city by air
candidates.pivotal: The Soviet blockade of West Berlin was lifted
start: usaf-history: official histories of the airlift
nara: records and photographs
wikipedia: Berlin Blockade

candidates.subject: The Battle of Britain
candidates.edge: Radar stations reporting to one control system, so fighters met raids instead of patrolling for them
candidates.pivotal: The German air campaign against Britain failed; the invasion was put off
start: uk-ogl: despatches and official histories (check each item's licence)
wikipedia: Battle of Britain
